To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 7.5 kyr long multi-proxy record of a raised bog in the southern Baltic coast of Poland reveals that the bog was affected by regional hydroclimatic shifts.
we have obtained a record of hydroclimate, vegetation succession, and fires during the Holocene from a southern Baltic bog that is the first such record from this region.

the Stązki record is a 7500 yr record of climate change in the southern Baltic that includes three phases: (a) moist conditions 550–3450 BC; (b) drier and warmer conditions 3450–600 BC; and (c) moist and cooler conditions from 600–1250 BC, and that the record is based on testate amoebas, pollen, plant macrofossil and charcoal analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
palaeohydrological and palaeoclimatic change in the southern Baltic, which has been poorly studied until now, and with the reconstruction of vegetation and land-use changes in this area.
palaeohydrology in the southern Baltic, but the data are also relevant for the understanding of the Holocene vegetation development in the Baltic region.
the development of a multi-proxy method for the reconstruction of environmental changes in the Baltic region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the climate of the southern Baltic region was relatively dry during the first half of the Holocene, but became more moist during the last 4000 yr.
the Holocene climate in the southern Baltic was characterized by a gradual shift from drier and warmer to wetter and colder conditions.
the southern Baltic region experienced a humid phase from 5500–1700 BC, followed by a drier phase until 600 BC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Stązki Bog record is a good proxy for the reconstruction of the Holocene climate in the southern Baltic.
the Stązki record provides a unique insight into the history of peat accumulation, vegetation and fires in the southern Baltic area during the Holocene.

the Stązki record provides evidence of the importance of regional climate and vegetation for local bog development and vegetation succession, as well as of the importance of local factors for regional climate and vegetation change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the southern Baltic region has experienced a similar climate to that of the northern Baltic, but with different vegetation.
testate amoebal analysis provides an excellent tool for the reconstruction of past environmental change, especially in the Baltic region where peatland vegetation and climate are closely linked.
testate amoebas, plant macrofossil and pollen data are highly congruent and can be used to reconstruct past hydroclimatic and environmental changes.
